The third release candidate of CoSky 8.0. It fixes what running rc.2 on a real cluster turned up, and keeps every promise of rc.1: from rc.1 to `8.0.0`, what [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning) lists only grows. CI ran rc.2 beside this release. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

Upgrading from rc.2 is a drop-in.

## Try it

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0-rc.3 --dev
```

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes. `8.0.0` follows once a release candidate has run in a real environment for two weeks without a serious problem. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you.

## Fixed

- **A directory the client cannot write snapshots to flooded the log.** A container user often has no home it may write to, so every snapshot under `~/.cosky` failed. Each failure logged a warning with its stack trace: one per change of a watched view.
  - **The default directory:** where it cannot be written, snapshots are now off. The client says so once, at info level, with how to keep them. A container without a persistent volume loses nothing by this, and a process on a host with a writable home keeps its snapshots as before.
  - **A directory set on purpose with `cosky.snapshot.dir`:** if it cannot be written, one warning says what to do. Writes are still tried, and the first that works again says so.
  - [Troubleshooting](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/troubleshooting#an-application-cannot-write-its-snapshots) explains. (#1325, #1327)

## Upgrading from rc.2

- **A drop-in.** Nothing in the contract changed, and the data in Redis is as before. Servers and applications can be upgraded in any order.
- **No default changes:** `cosky.snapshot.enabled` is still `true` and `cosky.snapshot.dir` still `~/.cosky`. Only an unwritable default directory now turns snapshots off.
- **An application that stays on rc.2 and logs `Could not write the snapshot`** can silence it with `COSKY_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED=false`, or point `COSKY_SNAPSHOT_DIR` at a volume. In Kubernetes, a snapshot outlives a restart only on a persistent volume, so a pod without one loses nothing without snapshots.

## Known limits

As in rc.2; see its [release notes](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/releases/tag/v8.0.0-rc.2).
